chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Paradise is prohibited to the slanderers, the conveyers of gossip.

key_terms.الْقَتَّاتِينَ: Slanderers; those who spread gossip and backbite
key_terms.الْمَشَّاءِينَ: The conveyers/walkers; those who actively carry and transmit
key_terms.بِالنَّمِيمَةِ: With gossip/namimah; the act of conveying words between people to cause enmity

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for slanderers and gossipers in Islam according to the hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies two distinct but related traits: 'al-qattatin' (those who tear apart unity through slander) and 'al-masha'un bi al-namimah' (those who actively walk about spreading it). This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, underscores the severity of namimah (gossip) in Shia jurisprudence as a major sin that severs social bonds and bars one from Paradise, reflecting the Quranic emphasis on preserving communal harmony.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yusuf Bin Aqeel, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Paradise is Prohibited unto the slanderers, the informers by the gossip’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yusuf ibn ‘Aqil from Muhammad ibn Qays from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
Entering paradise is prohibited to spies and gossip mongers.’”
